statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 10% while Stress is extreme at 80%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. NQ futures trade at 29,454.50, up 0.02%, in the middle of a 29,364.00 to 29,508.25 overnight band spanning roughly 0.49%. The band extended to a marginal new high this hour and that high was immediately rejected, while the low was faded earlier, so both extremes have produced retracements rather than the persistent no-pullback structure that defines tail conditions. VIX unchanged at 16.46 across the overnight hours confirms no tail repricing in options. Stress stays extreme because Brent above $100, a 10-year near its 2023 high at 4.84% and an active Gulf tanker conflict make the environment difficult even where mean reversion is intact, with producer prices today and consumer prices tomorrow still ahead. A narrow danger window is published around the 12:30 UTC producer price release and the 13:30 UTC cash open.
headline: NQ holds 29,454.50 mid-band after rejecting a marginal 29,508.25 overnight high, with VIX flat at 16.46 and Brent easing to $100.48, while a 4.84% 10-year keeps Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC PPI release
body: Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,454.50, up 5.75 points or 0.02%, inside an overnight range of 29,364.00 to 29,508.25. That band spans roughly 0.49% and extended by about 28 points at the top over the past hour, but the new high was rejected and price has returned to the middle of the range after the low was faded earlier. Both extremes have therefore now produced retracements, which is mean-reverting behaviour rather than the persistent directional efficiency that defines tail conditions. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 86.15 points or 0.29%, within a 29,334.40 to 29,563.60 range and beneath a 29,507.70 prior close. Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive but have stopped tightening. Brent trades at $100.48, easing 0.72% in what is described as profit-taking after US and Iranian forces exchanged strikes on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, and WTI is $95.62, down 0.45%. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.84%, marginally lower on the day after reaching its highest level since October 2023 on Wednesday, and the 2-year is 4.43%, down about 1.8 basis points; that combination points to term premium rather than a hawkish front-end repricing, and the overnight direction is a slight easing of the tightening impulse. VIX at 16.46, which closed 4.71% higher on Wednesday, has been unchanged through the overnight hours and remains the clearest counterweight: implied volatility is not pricing a discontinuity. Latest-session breadth is internally conflicted, with megacaps 1 of 8 higher on 2.59% dispersion as Meta rose 6.55% on an AI assistant launch while Alphabet fell 2.28%, set against semiconductors 5 of 7 higher on a 1.11% mean. Conflicting breadth of that kind lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. The scheduled path is dense: August producer prices, core producer prices and weekly jobless claims arrive at 12:30 UTC today, with consensus looking for a headline reacceleration toward the +5.3% annual pace from +4.7% in July, followed by August consumer prices at 12:30 UTC on 11 September and the 15-16 September FOMC meeting, where markets imply roughly 60% odds of a rate increase. Consistent with the standing method, an unreleased number raises Stress and uncertainty rather than observed Tail; only the price path after a release can establish tail conditions. Tail is therefore held at 10% and Stress at 80%. Confidence is 88% on live futures, index, yield, oil and volatility readings alongside a calendar and geopolitical picture corroborated across independent sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 05:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 22 of the 23 available slots, with one WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 7% to 20% and has settled into an 8-11% band overnight as retracements kept appearing at both ends of the range. Stress climbed from 76% to a sustained 80-83% as Brent broke $100 and the 10-year set fresh highs since October 2023. Confidence held between 87% and 89% throughout. The 10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path keeps Tail in a 10-14% range through the Asian and European sessions, lifts it to 20% in the 12:00 UTC release hour and a horizon peak of 22% in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-PPI repricing overlaps the US cash open, then decays it to 11-15% across the US afternoon and overnight into the CPI session. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in or at the top of the extreme band throughout because oil above $100, a 10-year near its 2023 high and an active Gulf shipping conflict are regime features that a single release does not clear. Confidence decays from 88% to 76% across the horizon as slots move further beyond the observed sample. A narrow danger window is published from 12:25 to 14:00 UTC.
